findings.title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 5-argument version
findings.description: The diff adds `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` alongside the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Ruby does not overload methods by arity. The later definition replaces the earlier one, so only the 4-argument form remains. Any existing call that passes `max_width` and `max_height` separately (5 positional arguments) now raises `ArgumentError`. Any 4-argument call that passes width and height as separate values binds the height to `opts`, which then fails when `opts[:allow_animation]` is read. The new call in `uploads_controller.rb` (`downsize(path, path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`) fits the new signature, but the old two-dimension form is broken. Either keep one method that accepts both forms, or rename the new one.

findings.title: Removed `OptimizedImage.dimensions` may break remaining callers
findings.description: The diff deletes `self.dimensions(width, height)`. This is a public class method, and the diff does not show whether other code calls it. Any remaining caller will raise `NoMethodError`. I could not confirm this without search access, so please grep for `OptimizedImage.dimensions` before merging.

findings.title: Existence of `FileHelper.is_image?` is unverified
findings.description: The new upload-resize block calls `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`. I could not confirm from the diff that this method exists with that name and signature. If it does not exist, the block raises `NoMethodError` for every upload that reaches it.
